name: instagram-mcp
description: Instagram (social): me, read_comments, reply_comment, read_mentions, analytics_post. Every tool maps

platform_mcp_instagram_access_token.title: PLATFORM_MCP_INSTAGRAM_ACCESS_TOKEN
platform_mcp_instagram_access_token.description: Instagram API with Facebook Login (host graph.facebook.com): a User or Page access token from Facebook Login for Business for a person with a role on the Facebook Page linked to the Instagram professional (Business or Creator) account, with instagram_basic, instagram_manage_comments, pages_read_engagement (and pages_show_list); sent as `Authorization: Bearer` (https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/comment-moderation).

platform_mcp_instagram_ig_user_id.title: PLATFORM_MCP_INSTAGRAM_IG_USER_ID
platform_mcp_instagram_ig_user_id.description: Instagram professional account id (IG User id, e.g. 17841405822304914) - GET /{page_id}?fields=instagram_business_account returns it. me and read_mentions call /<ig_user_id>. Env: PLATFORM_MCP_INSTAGRAM_IG_USER_ID.

tools.name: me
tools.description: GET /{ig_user_id}?fields=id,username,name,followers_count,media_count ('Get fields and edges on an Instagram Business or Creator Account').

tools.name: read_comments
tools.description: GET /{ig_media_id}/comments: 'Returns only top-level comments', 'Returns a maximum of 50 comments per query', 'Comments cannot be filtered by timestamp'; results are reverse chronological. page/limit are not sent (cursor paging).

tools.name: reply_comment
tools.description: 'To reply to a comment, send a POST request to the /<IG_COMMENT_ID>/replies endpoint ... with the message parameter set to your message text'; answers {id} of the new comment (instagram_manage_comments).

tools.name: read_mentions
tools.description: GET /{ig_user_id}/tags: 'IG Media objects in which an IG User has been tagged by another Instagram user' (private media are not returned). `since` goes to posted_after (ISO 8601, strict bound; 'This filtering capability is rolling out gradually'). Caption @mentions without a photo tag come only through the `mentions` webhook + mentioned_media / mentioned_comment lookups, which need the ids from that webhook. Cursor paging: page/limit are not sent.

tools.name: analytics_post
tools.description: GET /{ig_media_id}?fields=id,like_count,comments_count,permalink,timestamp,media_type (IG Media fields; like_count 'is omitted if the media owner has hidden like counts' when read indirectly). Reach / views / saves come from GET /{ig_media_id}/insights?metric=..., not used here. The runtime cannot compose a nested `metrics` object, so counts are top-level fields.
